newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says still backs strict EMU interpretation.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says still backs strict EMU interpretation.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday his Christian Social Union (CSU) supports a strict interpretation of the entry criteria for European Monetary Union (EMU).
In the text of a speech prepared for delivery at a party meeting, Waigel said Germany would fulfil the EMU criteria, despite doubts from some corners.
Waigel also said in the text that the degree of economic convergence by potential EMU participants would determine the EMU timetable, not the other way around.

"We stand by a strict interpretation of the entry criteria put down in the Maastricht Treaty," Waigel said, according to the prepared text. "Germany will meet the criteria despite doubts from some corners."
Waigel, however, did not give further details in the text of his speech, avoiding any reference to actual numbers contained in the Maastricht Treaty.
In recent days, he has stirred controversy by appearing to hedge on his view on the Maastricht requirement that budget deficits meet a reference value of three percent of gross domestic product.
